findings.detail: Earlier question M2-S23-T1 has the same problem. A legacy-code exploration subagent returns incomplete summaries, and the team chooses between an exact procedural step list and a goal with quality criteria (file paths, coverage of specific areas). The same reasoning from 1.3-S4 leads to the answer. Two wrong options also repeat earlier distractors. B (subagent builds on memory) repeats the shared-memory misconception, and C (exact Grep patterns and files to read) repeats the extended-step-list option. The rule allows at most one repeated wrong option.

blind_answer.reason: Per 1.3-S4, coordinator prompts should state research goals and quality criteria rather than step-by-step procedures, so the subagent can still adapt to the codebase. Option A does this by asking for file references, coverage of token expiry and error handling, and flagged uncertain findings. B is wrong because subagents keep no memory between invocations. C is the rigid procedure that removes adaptability. D cripples exploration.
